bc_the_basement.blurb: The Basement is a small steep sport crag in the Sanctuary section near Squamish. It has six bolted routes, all in the 5.11 and 5.12 range: two at 5.11 and four at 5.12. The wall overhangs, so the climbing is powerful and sustained, which is hard to find close by. It suits climbers already comfortable on hard sport routes; there is little here for anyone still working through the moderate grades. A neighbouring wall, the West Wing, has easier lines and works as a warm-up before heading up to this one.

bc_destruction_zone.blurb: Destruction Zone is a sport crag within Higgyland, the bolted cliff area at Powell River. It has six routes with a friendly spread: one near 5.7, four in the 5.10 range and one at 5.11. That makes it a good fit for climbers stepping up to the 5.10s who want a short, easy day without long walks between climbs. The neighbouring crags of Higgyland have more lines, so many parties combine this one with other sections of the cliff.

bc_the_leftorium.blurb: The Leftorium is a small, sloping crag on a lower tier of the Beach area in Kamloops. It has six routes: five sport and one trad, with grades from 5.8 up to 5.10. Several of the lines can also be used as top-rope climbs, and the bolted ones have intermediate anchors so a climber can stop short of the upper ledge. Two of the routes are recent additions and two older ones have been cleaned up. It is a modest wall for a short session, best suited to climbers working in the 5.8 to 5.10 range.

bc_left_3.blurb: Left is the northernmost wall in the Roche Lake climbing area near Kamloops, and it can be seen from the roadside pullout. It has six routes: four sport and two trad, some of which double as top-rope lines. Grades are mostly 5.8, with one 5.9 and one 5.10. That makes it one of the gentler walls at Roche Lake, a sensible place for newer leaders to start before moving to the steeper, harder sections. The walk from the road is short.

bc_sentinel_wall.blurb: Sentinel Wall sits high on Mount Sentinel above Castlegar in the West Kootenay. It is a steep face split across by a thick quartz dike, with six bolted routes, a few of them multipitch at four or five pitches. Five of the routes fall in the 5.10 range and one is a much harder 5.12 test piece. The walk in is long and the approach crosses a boulder field, so this is a committed outing rather than a quick roadside stop. It suits climbers comfortable on sustained 5.10 sport pitches.

bc_the_lounge.blurb: The Lounge is a small introductory sport crag in the Squamish Valley, north of Squamish. A few minutes uphill through forest from the gravel road brings you to six bolted routes on good stone, with a series of small roofs. Grades run from 5.7 up to 5.10, with a single route at each of 5.7, 5.8 and 5.9 and the remaining three at 5.10. The wall catches sun around midday. It suits newer leaders and a quick add-on to a day at the neighbouring Chuck Chuck Wall.
